primary_meaning: Divine revelation, authority, and guidance (the speech of God or Christ addressing humanity)
primary_basis: Psalm 29 (voice of the Lord over the waters, powerful and majestic)
Matthew 3:17 / Mark 1:11 / Luke 3:22 (voice from heaven at Jesus' baptism)
Revelation 1:10-15 (voice like a trumpet / many waters of the risen Christ)
Hebrews 3:7-15 / 4:7 (Today, if you hear his voice)

alternatives.meaning: Prophetic proclamation or the call to prepare for the Lord (especially the forerunner)
Inner guidance or conviction of the Holy Spirit / conscience
Manifestation of divine power or judgment
Human prayer, praise, testimony, or cry for justice

notes: In Christian biblical interpretation the term is not a rigid emblem like 'lamb' or 'rock,' yet a clear primary association exists with God's (or Christ's) communicative presence and authority. Other senses appear frequently but are secondary or contextual rather than competing primary symbols. No single technical 'symbol of the voice' is codified in creeds or standard handbooks beyond this dominant divine-speech usage.
